content.text:
Enough evidence to write. The score model says a uniform 10% cut on every band is worth +0.021, and the lowest rows are still the six wide-C 7x7/14x14 rows (S 0.69-0.71), so most ideas target D's wide-C kernel terms the r9 stamps exposed: the W1 DRAM stream in phase A, the 48 KB latency-bound GEMM2 stages, the h+g store bytes, the 2-tile GEMM1 tails, and the ~105 clk per-instruction MMA floor at N <= 128.

### Notes
The LEADER GAP table is stale: it backs out a 0.6904 leader, below our 0.7359, so every "leader time" there is slower than ours. The stories below target the live first place (0.7435, +0.0076 of mean, about a uniform -3.6%). Idea arithmetic uses r9 rented stamps at 8,768 (phase A 5.5-7, sync1 8.1, GEMM1 end ~20, sync2 22.8, end 30.7 us) and the r9 G finding that a 1SM kind::f16 MMA instruction costs ~105 clk whatever N <= 128. Ideas 1, 2, 5 and 6 compose inside D's tc_kernel; 8-10 are long shots with 10-minute microbench gates. Precision: every idea keeps fp16/fp32-accumulate single roundings except idea 1's per-image rescale of a resident fp16 W2 (one extra rounding of W2, estimated 65% -> ~75% of atol; must be logged over 10 seeded rounds, fallback rebuilds A from fp32 W2).

[
{"title": "Token-balanced N=256 GEMM1 tiles plus a resident per-CTA W2 slice for GEMM2 (g removed, B-only deep ring)", "family": "resident-A GEMM2", "design": "Keep D's single cooperative tcgen05 kernel and swap-AB orientation, but decouple GEMM1 tiles from images: each of 147 CTAs takes one hidden tile (128 rows) x ~256 tokens (16,384: 12 hidden tiles x 12.25 token groups of 256 from 3136 tokens; 32,768: 24 x 6.1; 8,768 keeps 96 tiles of N=112). Per-(image,k) sumsq goes by red.add into a [B][4C] fp32 array zeroed in phase A (sc_kernel already does this); the epilogue stores h16 only. After sync 2 every CTA computes mean_b for its images (3072 sqrt+sum, one load round), then owns one (c-tile, k-slice) unit: it TMA-loads its fp16 W2 slice (128 c x 512 k = 128 KB) into smem ONCE during the sync-2 wait window (no dependency), rescales it in place by s_b[k] per image (64K fp16 elements / 512 threads, ~0.3 us), and streams only B = h[k-slice][tokens] through an 8-12 deep ring of 7-26 KB stages (one image per tile at 7x7, N=56; 208 at 14x14), single accumulator, then the usual split-K red.add. KS=6 at C=768 (36 units x 4 token groups = 144 CTAs), KS=3 or 6 at C=384.", "p_expert": 0.3, "effect": "GEMM1 phase: one wave of N=256 tiles at the MMA ideal (12 k-blocks x 4 x 128 clk = 3.2 us mainloop) with an h-only epilogue (~5 us) instead of 2 tiles x (1.4 + 8.1) + 12 us tail at 16,384 and 264 tiles = 1.8 waves at 32,768: -10 us on both. GEMM2: stage bytes 48 KB -> 7-26 KB so the ring can be 8-12 deep (192 KB in flight at 16 KB stages covers a 1 us round trip), per-stage 0.7 us -> ~0.15-0.3 us: 8,768 GEMM2 8 -> ~3-4 us, 32,768 ~20 -> ~8. g removal saves ~1.2 us per tile wave and the per-image s_b needs no in-ring work. Rented targets: 16,384 50.9 -> ~40, 32,768 65 -> ~52, 16,768 43.5 -> ~35, 8,768 32.4 -> ~27, 8,384 33.4 -> ~28, 2,768 24 -> ~22. At D's 1.2-1.3 ratio that is S ~0.74-0.76 on all six rows, about +0.015 of mean. The same resident-A GEMM2 replaces G's K3+G2 at 8,320 / 4,96 (4 launches -> 3).", "risk": "Double rounding of W2 (fp16(fp16(W2)*s)) may push the C=768 rows from 65% to ~75-80% of atol: must be logged over 10 seeded rounds; fallback is rebuilding A from fp32 W2 through a 32 KB staging ring (ingest-bound, ~1.7 us per image per CTA). Smem: 128 KB resident A + ring must fit 227 KB alongside stats and barriers. Red volume is unchanged only if KS stays <= 6; KS=12 would double the red.add bytes (58 MB at 32,768).", "test": "10-minute probe with D's GEMM2 ring: 148 CTAs, cold L2, resident 128 KB A, B-only 16 KB stages at depth 4 / 8 / 12, measure us per 64-k stage vs the current 0.7 us; refute if a 12-deep B-only ring is not below 0.3 us per stage."},
{"title": "Convert W1 inside the GEMM1 ring (fp32 TMA boxes, converter warps, LN-fold row sums accumulated on the fly): no W1 pass in phase A", "family": "zero weight pass", "design": "Phase A keeps only the plane conv (and the out = x + b2 prefill). GEMM1 CTAs TMA-load their 128-row W1 slice as fp32 32 KB boxes (64 k per stage) into a 2-deep staging buffer; 4 converter warps multiply by lnw[c], cvt.rn.f16x2, write the SW128 K-major fp16 A stage (16 KB, 4 deep) and accumulate the per-row sum u[k] of the rounded values in registers (needed for the LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + v), then fence.proxy.async and arrive; the TMA for the staging buffer is issued by a separate producer warp so no arriving thread has loads in flight. The deferred fp16 W2 pass stays as in r9 (or is replaced by idea 1's resident slice). Smem during GEMM1: 2 x 32 + 4 x 16 + B ring 3 x 32 = 224 KB (freed before GEMM2).", "p_expert": 0.35, "effect": "Removes the 9.4 MB fp32 W1 read + 4.7 MB fp16 write from the phase-A critical path: sync 1 moves from 8.1 to ~5.3 us at 8,768 (r9 ablation without W1: 5.3-5.9). GEMM1 per-stage ingest grows from 16 KB to 32 KB of A (~400 vs 200 clk at 80 B/clk) against a 420 clk MMA floor per stage, so the mainloop grows by 0.6-1.1 us per tile. Net -1.5..-2.5 us on every C=768 row and -1 on C=384 (rented), about +0.004-0.006 of mean.", "risk": "Converter warps gating stages the way smem-g did (0.8 us per stage) if they cannot run 2 stages ahead; W1 is re-read from L2 once per token group (4-6x at balanced tiles: 40-56 MB of L2 traffic, fine for L2 but it must not land on the per-SM ingest cap). u[k] summation order changes vs the shipped path: re-log precision.", "test": "Stamp probe at 8,768: GEMM1 mainloop per stage with in-ring conversion vs fp16 TMA A; refute if the converted ring exceeds 600 clk per 64-k stage or if sync 1 does not land before 6 us."},
{"title": "TF32 GEMM1 straight from fp32 memory through TFLOAT32 tensor maps (zero conversion, fp32 d)", "family": "zero weight pass", "design": "kind::tf32 for GEMM1 only: A = fp32 W1 slice via a TFLOAT32 TMA map (round-to-nearest, H14), B = d stored fp32 [C][tokens] by the conv (2x bytes, 1.2-5 MB), 32 KB A + 16-32 KB B per 64-k stage, 3 stages. u[k] = rowsum(lnw * tf32(W1)) computed by spare warps reading each landed A stage (16 elements per thread per stage, read-only so no gating). GEMM2 stays fp16 (deferred W2 pass or idea 1). Precision class: r5 E logged TF32 at 59-67% of atol.", "p_expert": 0.5, "effect": "Same phase-A saving as idea 2 (-2.5..-3 us at sync 1) with no converter warps. But kind::tf32 issues K=8 instructions: if the ~105 clk floor is per instruction, a 64-k stage costs 8 x 105 = 840 clk instead of 420, i.e. +2.6 us per 12-block tile at 7x7 (N <= 128), which cancels the gain there; at N >= 208 (14x14, balanced tiles) the tf32 ideal is 2x the f16 ideal: 12 k-blocks x 8 x 128 = 12.3k clk = 6.4 us vs 3.2. Net: roughly a wash at 7x7, -1..-2 us at 14x14 only if the floor is bytes-bound rather than instruction-bound. Low expected value unless the microbench says the floor halves for K=8.", "risk": "The per-instruction floor doubles the mainloop; fp32 d doubles the B bytes; the ledger's I2/I20 revisit clause was written before the floor was known.", "test": "G's MMA microbench (10 min): kind::tf32 128xNx8 instruction throughput at N = 64 / 112 / 128 / 256 with smem-resident operands; proceed only if clk per instruction is <= 60 at N <= 128."},
{"title": "Two CTAs per SM for the wide-C kernel (256 threads, <= 110 KB smem, grid 296) so one CTA's epilogue and latency chains overlap the other's mainloop", "family": "occupancy", "design": "Launch D's tc_kernel cooperatively with 296 CTAs of 256 threads (8 warps: 1 TMA, 1 MMA, 6 epilogue), smem 110 KB each (phase A plane units halve per CTA; GEMM1 ring 32 KB stages x 3; GEMM2 B-only stages from idea 1 or 48 KB x 2), TMEM split 256 columns per CTA (allocate 256), registers <= 128 per thread. Work tables double the unit count (half-size token groups).", "p_expert": 0.3, "effect": "Mechanisms: (a) if the ~105 clk per-MMA floor is per issuing CTA (an A-fetch pipeline latency, as the accumulator-independence test suggests) two CTAs double the tensor rate at N <= 128: -1.3 us per GEMM1 tile at 8,768; (b) each CTA's post-accumulator epilogue (3-8 us, store- and issue-bound) overlaps the co-resident CTA's mainloop and phase-A chains: the 1-CTA kernel leaves the SM idle during every wait; the portal amplified latency-tolerance gains on #88 (+16.7% portal vs +6.7% bench). Expected -8..-15% on the six wide-C rows if (a) holds, -3..-6% from (b) alone.", "risk": "If the floor is per SM nothing changes on the MMA side; 2 x 48 KB GEMM2 rings are shallower (worse) unless idea 1 lands; the epilogue at 256 threads is slower per tile (r6 showed 8 warps issue-bound) so two tiles must genuinely overlap; cooperative residency check must pass with 2 CTAs/SM at 110 KB.", "test": "G's MMA microbench at 2 CTAs/SM (10 min): per-instruction clk at N=64/112 with 148 vs 296 CTAs; if throughput doubles, build; otherwise only test (b) by stamping a 2-CTA build of phase A + GEMM1 at 8,384."},
{"title": "Asynchronous bulk reduce-add and bulk stores: cp.reduce.async.bulk for the GEMM2 split-K drain, TMA store for h, warps never wait on global writes", "family": "async stores", "design": "GEMM2 epilogue: tcgen05.ld the accumulator, add nothing (out is prefilled with x + b2), write the fp32 tile [128 c][tokens] into smem, then one elected thread issues cp.reduce.async.bulk (.add.f32) per contiguous row segment: at 14x14 each (b, c) row is 784 B (16-B aligned), at 7x7 a (b, c) row is 196 B so use 1-D segments spanning 4 consecutive c rows of one image (784 B) for whole-image tiles, padding the last partial row with scalar red.add. GEMM1 epilogue: h16 staged tile goes out with cp.async.bulk.tensor store (evict_last hint) instead of STG.128 so the epilogue warps move to the next tile immediately and wait_group only before reusing the staging buffer.", "p_expert": 0.35, "effect": "Replaces 16K-32K scalar red.add per unit (H measured ~4 of 7.4 us; D's drain+red is 3.7-8 us per row) with ~100 bulk instructions issued by one thread: the drain term drops to ~1-2 us (-2..-5 us per wide-C row, largest at 32,768 with 2 units per CTA). The h bulk store overlaps the next tile's mainloop where a CTA has 2 tiles (16,384 / 32,768) and shortens the store burst. About +0.004-0.006 of mean.", "risk": "Bulk reduce ordering vs the prefill: the prefill must be visible before any reduce (it is, before sync 2); 7x7 row segments crossing c boundaries are fine (adds into our own output) only inside one image's [C][49] block; L2 reduce throughput for bulk add is unmeasured on B200.", "test": "Microbench (10 min): 148 CTAs each reduce-adding a 128 x 112 fp32 tile from smem into a 1.2 MB buffer after the flush, bulk vs coalesced scalar red.add; refute if bulk is not >= 2x faster."},
{"title": "L2 eviction-priority hints on the weight stream and the hidden: fp32 W reads evict_first, fp16 W'/h/g stores evict_last, x plane copies evict_first", "family": "cache hints", "design": "Phase A: load fp32 W1/W2 with ld.global.L2::cache_hint + createpolicy evict_first (the lines are dead after conversion), store W' fp16 with evict_last (read by every GEMM CTA), 1-D bulk plane copies of x with the evict_first policy operand. GEMM1 epilogue: h/g STG with evict_last (re-read by GEMM2 within ~10 us). GEMM2 B TMA loads with evict_first (read once). out prefill and red.add default.", "p_expert": 0.5, "effect": "Under the dirty-L2 flush every allocated line forces a write-back; the 18.9 MB of dead fp32 weight lines marked evict_first become the victims for the 9.4 MB W' and 9.6 MB h+g allocations instead of dirty flush lines, so the epilogue store burst (2.3 us per tile wave at 6-7 TB/s) and the W' write run at L2 rates: -1..-2 us per wide-C row (-3..-5%), ~+0.003 of mean. Verified mechanism on #84/#85 (+3-13%); untested in D (card 6.7).", "risk": "Refuted on #38 at some sizes; evict_last on h could pin lines and hurt the x/out streams at 32,768 (28 MB total, far below 126 MB, so unlikely); no effect if the L2 replacement ignores priority for TMA writes.", "test": "Knob build of r9 D with the hints, interleaved x3 against the parent in one container on 8,768 / 16,384 / 32,768; keep whichever hint set wins by > 0.5 us."},
{"title": "Conv inside GEMM1 clusters with a DSMEM d all-gather: no sync 1, no d round trip, B operand resident for the whole K", "family": "cluster conv", "design": "For rows whose (image, hidden-tile-group) unit count fits one wave (2,768: 2 images x 3 groups of 8 tiles = 48 CTAs; 8,768 with 2-image units: 96 CTAs), launch clusters of 8 CTAs per (image group, 8 hidden tiles). Each CTA bulk-copies the x planes of 96 of the 768 channels (19 KB per image), runs the 7x7 conv for them (230K FMA, ~0.9 us), exchanges 2 floats per token of LN partial stats through DSMEM, normalises, converts to fp16 and writes its 96-channel slab of the MN-major B tile into all 8 CTAs' smem (st.shared::cluster, 11 KB per remote CTA per image). After a cluster barrier each CTA holds the full B operand (768 ch x 56 tokens fp16 = 86 KB) resident and streams only its A slice; GEMM1 epilogue and GEMM2 as now, with sync 2 as the only grid barrier.", "p_expert": 0.15, "effect": "At 2,768 removes phase A (5.5 us) + sync 1 release (1-1.5) + the post-sync B TMA rounds, replacing them with 0.9 us conv + ~2.6 us all-gather (75 KB per CTA at the measured 13.5-18.5 B/clk/SM): -3..-4 us of 24 (S 0.72 -> ~0.76). At 8,768 the 2-image units need 5 us of all-gather, so the gain is ~1 us; 14x14 rows need 147 KB per CTA of DSMEM traffic (5 us) and do not pay. A specialist for 2,768 only unless DSMEM is faster than H13 measured.", "risk": "DSMEM all-gather rate (H13: ~12-18 B/clk/SM) is the whole bet; clusters of 8 in a cooperative launch need cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters >= units; the constraint allows clusters only where a GEMM tile needs them (here the B operand assembly), so get the operator's reading first.", "test": "Microbench (10 min): 8-CTA cluster all-gather of 8 x 11 KB slabs into every CTA's smem, 48 clusters, measure us; refute if > 2 us."},
{"title": "A operand from TMEM: keep the W1' hidden-tile slice resident in tensor memory and stream only B", "family": "TMEM-A MMA", "design": "tcgen05.mma has an [a-tmem] form. For kind::f16, K=768 needs 48 chunks x 8 columns = 384 TMEM columns for a 128-row A slice, leaving 128 columns for an N <= 128 fp32 accumulator (exactly 512). Load the slice once per CTA via the fp16 TMA ring + tcgen05.cp (smem -> TMEM, async), then every GEMM1 tile of that hidden tile on this CTA streams only d (B, 7-21 KB per stage). Order the tile table so CTAs with 2 tiles (16,384 / 32,768) get the same hidden rows twice.", "p_expert": 0.1, "effect": "Two possible wins: (a) the ~105 clk per-instruction floor at N <= 128 is plausibly the smem A fetch (4 KB per instruction, ~39 B/clk); from TMEM it may drop toward the ideal N/2 clk: 48 instructions at N=112 go from 5.1k to 2.7k clk (-1.3 us per tile at 7x7); (b) the 192 KB A ingest disappears for a CTA's second tile (-1.2 us at 32,768 / 16,384). Up to -2..-3 us per C=768 row (~+0.004 of mean), more if combined with idea 1's balanced tiles at N=128.", "risk": "The A-in-TMEM layout for 16-bit types must match what the MMA expects (PTX ISA table for .kind::f16 A in TMEM); tcgen05.cp shapes and the 512-column budget leave no room for a second accumulator; the floor may be elsewhere (B fetch, issue), in which case only (b) remains.", "test": "G's one-CTA MMA microbench (10 min): kind::f16 128xNx16 with A from TMEM at N = 64 / 112 / 128, clk per instruction vs the 105-107 measured with smem A; proceed only if < 80 clk at N=112."},
{"title": "k-stationary one-barrier kernel for M <= 128 rows (2,768): the CTA keeps its 128 hidden rows in smem across the GRN wait and does both GEMMs", "family": "k-stationary", "design": "24 CTAs (one per 128-row hidden tile) plus 124 helper CTAs for the conv. Phase A as now (conv units, W2 conversion by the helpers). Then CTA k: GEMM1 128 x 98 tokens x K=768 with A streamed (or resident, 192 KB), epilogue writes h16 (128 x 98 = 25 KB) into its own smem and the per-(image,k) sumsq into a [B][4C] array, then arrives on a self-resetting counter; after all 24 arrive (flat counter, 0.9 us) each CTA computes mean_b, scales its smem h tile by s_b[k] in place (12.5K elements, ~0.05 us), and runs GEMM2 as A = fp16 W2[:, k-tile] (6 c-tiles x 128 x 128 fp16 = 32 KB each, streamed from the W2' scratch) x B = the resident h tile, draining 6 partial tiles with red.add into the prefilled out (24 partials x 98 x 768 x 4 B = 7.2 MB, ~1.7 us at 4.2 TB/s).", "p_expert": 0.2, "effect": "2,768 rented 24 -> ~16.5 us (phase A 5.5 + GEMM1 ~4.5 incl. the N=98 MMA floor + counter 1 + GEMM2 6 x 8 instructions ~1 + drain ~2 + ramps): portal ~30.7 -> ~21-22, S 0.72 -> ~0.80, about +0.005 of mean from one row. Does not transfer to 8,768 (24 partials x 392 tokens = 29 MB of red.add, 7 us) unless the k-tile is 512 wide, which puts GEMM1 on 6 CTAs.", "risk": "Only 24 CTAs carry both GEMMs (GEMM1 mainloop at N=98 is floor-bound, 48 x 106 clk = 2.6 us; helpers are idle after phase A); a cluster-of-4 split-K for GEMM1 adds a 50 KB DSMEM reduce (~1.3 us) and does not help GEMM2's partial count. Worth one row.", "test": "Stub probe (10 min): 24 CTAs running the GEMM1 tile + counter + 6 GEMM2 slices on cold L2 at 2,768 shapes; refute if the stub exceeds 12 us without phase A."},
